ut_kitchen_the.blurb: The Kitchen is a small alcove crag in Rock Canyon above Provo, right beside the main canyon trail, which makes it the busiest wall in the canyon. The climbing is short, roughly 20 feet, and mostly gentle: about eleven lines mixing trad, a few sport routes, one top-rope problem and a couple of boulder problems, from easy 5.5 terrain up through the low 5.10s, with a sport line at 5.11 and boulder problems around V2 and V3. Anchors at the top let you set up top ropes on several lines quickly, so it works well for first-timers and short sessions. Expect company on good days.
ut_kitchen_the.parking_note: Leave the car in the main Rock Canyon lot, then walk up the main trail to the alcove.

ut_dark_lands_mid_canyon.blurb: Dark Lands is the middle stretch of Cove Wash, a tight sandstone canyon near Saint George and Santa Clara. Eleven short routes, mostly sport with two trad lines, run from an easy 5.5 up to 5.11, with the bulk of them in the 5.10 range and a handful of moderates for warming up. Climbers describe the stone as solid, though a few small flakes and nubs deserve a look before you trust them. First bolts tend to sit high, so a stick clip is handy, and the anchors can be reached from the rim, which makes top-roping straightforward. Routes are brief enough to link many in one day.
ut_dark_lands_mid_canyon.approach: Walk up the wash past the Bad Ethics area and over a chockstone, or follow the rim a few hundred yards and make an easy fourth-class downclimb into the canyon.

ut_1_begay_boulder.blurb: Begay Boulder is a single large block sitting just off the road at the Big Water boulders in the Glen Canyon area of south-central Utah. It anchors the first roadside pullout, so the walk is close to nothing. Eleven problems cover everything from very easy up to V5, with a fairly even spread through the middle grades. Its draw is the pocketed, overhanging stone, which is unusual for this zone, and the hardest line is a pocket problem that climbers rate among the best here. It is a handy stop for a quick session with pads, and a base for reaching nearby boulder groups.
ut_1_begay_boulder.parking_note: Drive 2.6 miles along NP230 and pull off at the two large boulders on the left; the bigger one has the name Begay carved into it.

ut_chip_and_dale.blurb: Chip and Dale is a small boulder zone in New Joe's, the hillside-and-canyon sector of Joe's Valley in central Utah, a little farther up the road than the Anarchy area. Eleven sandstone problems here skew hard: one around V3 and another near V5, then a cluster in the V7 to V9 range, including two well-known V7 lines. It suits strong boulderers more than newcomers. The sandstone is porous and loses strength when damp, so dry conditions matter a great deal here.

ut_bungalow_the.blurb: The Bungalow is a compact sport crag in Parley's Canyon on the east side of Salt Lake City, tucked in as an add-on to the main Parley's walls. Routes are short, but the rock is good and the climbing is moderate and fun. Ten sport lines and one trad line span from about 5.6 to 5.10, with the most routes around 5.8 and 5.9, so it suits newer leaders and anyone after a quick, easy tick session. Tree cover gives the belay area decent shade. Reaching the base involves a short scramble down an easy staircase feature.

ut_impact_zone_wall_the.blurb: The Impact Zone Wall is a steep, overhanging face of cobble in Box Canyon at Maple Canyon, central Utah, facing the Ammo Dump wall from the other side of the canyon. It holds eleven sport routes and nothing easy: two around 5.11, a big cluster at 5.12, and one at 5.13. The cobble is described as great rock, and the wall is aimed at strong climbers working powerful, sustained lines rather than anyone looking for warm-ups.
